label: Leader
summary: The leading character a text names, such as the head of a holy order.
details: Vanilla builds holy order names from the leader's first name ("[name]ites").

label: Lease contract type
summary: A lease contract type the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is the kind of lease contract the text is about. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Left artifact
summary: An artifact the game fills in for the text or window being shown, named LEFT_ARTIFACT.
details: Going by its name, it is the first of two artifacts a text compares or talks about (the other side being RIGHT). The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Left character
summary: The first of the two characters a message is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the texts of relation messages (friend, best friend, rival), always together with RIGHT_CHARACTER: both are written with .Self and handed to a relation's reason text. Which of the two is which comes from the message the game is showing.

label: Left doctrine
summary: A doctrine the game fills in for the text or window being shown, named LEFT_DOCTRINE.
details: Going by its name, it is the first of two doctrines a text compares. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Left faith
summary: A faith the game fills in for the text or window being shown, named LEFT_FAITH.
details: Going by its name, it is the first of two faiths a text compares or talks about. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Left rite
summary: A rite the game fills in for the text or window being shown, named LEFT_RITE.
details: Going by its name, it is the first of two rites a text compares. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Left tenet
summary: A tenet (a religious principle of a faith) the game fills in for the text or window being shown, named LEFT_TENET.
details: Going by its name, it is the first of two tenets a text compares. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Message title
summary: The title a notification message is about.
details: Vanilla's messages use it, for example, for the title inherited or lost, a mercenary company or holy order that was dismissed, or one of the titles whose province an epidemic spread to. When a message names two titles, RIGHT_TITLE is the second.

label: Legend
summary: The legend a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's legend effect texts use it, for example when its quality changes or a character becomes its owner.

label: Legend seed
summary: The legend seed (a legend in the making, the basis a ruler can found a legend from) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla writes it as its name for a character, then its quality and type in brackets.

label: Legend type
summary: A legend type the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is the kind of legend the window or text is about. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Legitimacy level
summary: A legitimacy level the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is one step of the legitimacy scale. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it under this name.

label: Legitimacy type
summary: A legitimacy type the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is the kind of legitimacy the text is about. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Lifestyle
summary: The lifestyle a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the message that a new perk can be unlocked in a lifestyle, and in the condition text "Has the ... lifestyle".

label: Less than or equal (decimal)
summary: Whether the first decimal number is smaller than or equal to the second.
details: CFixedPoint is the game's fixed-point decimal number, used for most script values. Vanilla uses it to choose between two texts depending on a scheme success chance or a value read from a war.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than or equal (float)
summary: Whether the first float number is smaller than or equal to the second.
details: A float is an ordinary decimal number as computers store it. Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name and its siblings, it is the float version of the less-than-or-equal check.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than or equal (whole)
summary: Whether the first whole number is smaller than or equal to the second.
details: Vanilla uses it in GUI files to show something only while an age is at most 1. Whole numbers in a call are written like '(int32)1'.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than or equal (unsigned)
summary: Whether the first unsigned whole number is smaller than or equal to the second.
details: An unsigned number is a whole number that cannot be negative. Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the unsigned version of the less-than-or-equal check.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than zero
summary: Whether a whole number is below zero.
details: It is a shortcut that expands to a less-than comparison against '(int32)0'. The game's own description says it tests whether the number is greater than zero, which contradicts its name and its expansion; the expansion is what counts. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Less than zero (decimal)
summary: Whether a decimal number is below zero.
details: A shortcut for comparing the value with '(CFixedPoint)0' using the decimal less-than check. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Less than (decimal)
summary: Whether the first decimal number is smaller than the second.
details: CFixedPoint is the game's fixed-point decimal number. Vanilla uses it in the HUD to show an element only while a balance or the player's gold is below 0, and in a map icon text to pick a wording when the player has less of a currency than a province needs.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than (float)
summary: Whether the first float number is smaller than the second.
details: A float is an ordinary decimal number as computers store it. Vanilla uses it in the Great Holy War window to show something while the war's strength progress is under 50.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than (whole)
summary: Whether the first whole number is smaller than the second.
details: Vanilla uses it often in texts and GUI files, for example to pick a wording when an accolade has no unspent points left.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Less than (unsigned)
summary: Whether the first unsigned whole number is smaller than the second.
details: An unsigned number is a whole number that cannot be negative. Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the unsigned version of the less-than check.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Is live mode
summary: Whether the game is running in a mode called live mode.
details: Going by its name, it tells the interface whether it is in live mode. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Localized text
summary: The text for a localization key, in the player's language.
details: Vanilla builds the key on the fly, for example by joining 'animal_type_' with a variable to look up an animal's name in event text. Vanilla's Polish helper macros compare its result with the key itself, which suggests a missing key gives the key back; the game does not document this.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The localization key to look up.
fields.values: a text key, often built with Concatenate

label: Number as text
summary: Turns a long whole number into text.
details: Going by its name, it turns a long whole number into characters so it can be put in a text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The number to turn into text.

label: Men-at-arms type
summary: A men-at-arms type (a kind of professional regiment) the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Vanilla texts write it with the type's name, icon key or base type name, for example in a line naming the regiment type in a combat tooltip or in a list entry of men-at-arms a ruler could get access to. The game sets it to the type the text is about.

label: Second men-at-arms type
summary: The second men-at-arms type in a text that names two.
details: Vanilla's one use is in the realm window: "Their men-at-arms are mostly [type] and [type 2]".

label: Mercenary company
summary: A mercenary company the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is the mercenary company the window or text is about. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Modifier item
summary: A modifier entry the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is one modifier in a list shown in the interface. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Line if condition
summary: Gives a localization text followed by a line break, but only when a condition is true.
details: It is a shortcut for adding the text when the condition holds and then a newline, and nothing at all when the condition is false. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: LocKey
fields.text: The localization key of the text.

label: Paragraph if condition
summary: Gives a localization text followed by an empty line, but only when a condition is true.
details: Like MakeLineIf, but it ends with a double line break, so a blank line separates it from what follows. When the condition is false nothing is added. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: LocKey
fields.text: The localization key of the text.

label: Scope from yes/no
summary: Turns a true or false value into a script scope.
details: Going by its name, it wraps a boolean so it can be handed to script functions that expect a scope. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Scope from flag
summary: Turns a flag name into a script scope.
details: Going by its name, it wraps a flag so it can be handed to script functions that expect a scope. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Scope from value
summary: Turns a number into a script scope.
details: Going by its name, it wraps a number so it can be handed to script functions that expect a scope. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Map editor has game map mode
summary: Whether the map editor currently has a game map mode.
details: Vanilla uses it only in the map editor's dockable map mode selector, as the checked state of an entry. The game documents nothing more.

label: Larger decimal
summary: The larger of two decimal numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it to keep a displayed value from going below zero: the court position window shows the greater of a travel aptitude and 0.

label: Larger float
summary: The larger of two float numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it so a maximum value in the ledger is never below 1: it takes the larger of an army's soldier count and 1.

label: Larger whole number
summary: The larger of two whole numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it in a notification to show the larger of 0 and the days left until a diplomatic item times out, so the shown number does not go below 0.

label: Larger unsigned number
summary: The larger of two unsigned whole numbers.
details: An unsigned number cannot be negative. Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the unsigned version of the larger-of check.

label: Smaller decimal
summary: The smaller of two decimal numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it in the Christian church window: a segmented progress bar gets the smaller of the Great Schism progress value and its threshold value, so the bar value never goes above the threshold.

label: Smaller float
summary: The smaller of two float numbers.
details: Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the float version of the smaller-of check.

label: Smaller whole number
summary: The smaller of two whole numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger to take at most one entry of a list: the smaller of 1 and the list's size, which gives 0 for an empty list and 1 otherwise.

label: Smaller unsigned number
summary: The smaller of two unsigned whole numbers.
details: An unsigned number cannot be negative. Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the unsigned version of the smaller-of check.

label: Remainder (decimal)
summary: The remainder after dividing the first decimal number by the second.
details: Going by its name, it is the modulo operation on the game's fixed-point decimal numbers. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Remainder (2D vector)
summary: The remainder of dividing one two-part vector by another.
details: A 2D vector is a pair of decimal numbers such as a screen position. Going by its name, the remainder is taken part by part. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Remainder (3D vector)
summary: The remainder of dividing one three-part vector by another.
details: A 3D vector is three decimal numbers such as a position in space. Going by its name, the remainder is taken part by part. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Remainder (4D vector)
summary: The remainder of dividing one four-part vector by another.
details: A 4D vector is four decimal numbers, for example a color with transparency. Going by its name, the remainder is taken part by part. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Remainder (float)
summary: The remainder after dividing the first float number by the second.
details: Going by its name, it is the modulo operation on float numbers. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Remainder (whole)
summary: The remainder after dividing the first whole number by the second.
details: Vanilla uses it in a shared backgrounds file: the entry's position in its list modulo 2 is compared with 0, which picks every second entry.

label: Remainder (unsigned)
summary: The remainder after dividing the first unsigned whole number by the second.
details: An unsigned number cannot be negative. Going by its name, it is the modulo operation on such numbers. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Months per year
summary: The number of months in a year.
details: A whole number the game provides so texts and windows do not hard-code it. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Multiply (decimal)
summary: The first decimal number times the second.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a chance as a percentage: a character's chance of victory in a tournament is multiplied by 100.

label: Multiply (2D vector)
summary: Multiplies two two-part vectors.
details: A 2D vector is a pair of decimal numbers such as a screen position or size. Going by its name, the parts are multiplied. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Multiply (3D vector)
summary: Multiplies two three-part vectors.
details: A 3D vector is three decimal numbers such as a position in space. Going by its name, the parts are multiplied. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Multiply (4D vector)
summary: Multiplies two four-part vectors.
details: A 4D vector is four decimal numbers, for example a color with transparency. Going by its name, the parts are multiplied. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Multiply (float)
summary: The first float number times the second.
details: Vanilla uses it in GUI files to scale values for bars and progress: a construction progress times 100, or a combat advantage times -1 to flip its direction.

label: Multiply (whole)
summary: The first whole number times the second.
details: Vanilla uses it once, in the text of a merit bar marker.

label: Multiply (unsigned)
summary: The first unsigned whole number times the second.
details: An unsigned number cannot be negative. Going by its name, it is the multiplication for such numbers. Vanilla does not use it.

label: New relation level
summary: The level a house relation moves to, in a text that also names the old one.
details: Vanilla's one use: the relation improves or worsens "from [old level] to [new level]".

label: Do nothing
summary: A dummy function that does nothing.
details: The game describes it as a no-operation placeholder callback. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not both
summary: Whether at least one of the two values is false.
details: It is false only when both values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not both (2)
summary: Whether at least one of 2 values is false.
details: The same as Nand: it is false only when both values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not all (3)
summary: Whether at least one of 3 values is false.
details: It is false only when all three values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not all (4)
summary: Whether at least one of 4 values is false.
details: It is false only when all four values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not all (5)
summary: Whether at least one of 5 values is false.
details: It is false only when all five values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not all (6)
summary: Whether at least one of 6 values is false.
details: It is false only when all six values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not all (7)
summary: Whether at least one of 7 values is false.
details: It is false only when all seven values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not all (8)
summary: Whether at least one of 8 values is false.
details: It is false only when all eight values are true. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Non-breaking space
summary: A space that never wraps to a new line.
details: Going by its name, a non-breaking space. Vanilla puts it between an icon and a name, so the icon is meant to stay on the same line as the name.

label: Change sign
summary: The value with its sign flipped: positive becomes negative and the other way round.
details: It is a shortcut that subtracts the value from 0 as a decimal number. Vanilla does not call it (the word only appears in plain text).

label: Change sign (decimal)
summary: A decimal number with its sign flipped.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tax window to show a tax change with the opposite sign when removing a vassal.

label: Change sign (float)
summary: A float number with its sign flipped.
details: Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the float version of changing a sign.

label: Change sign (whole)
summary: A whole number with its sign flipped.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tax window to show the change in levies with the opposite sign when removing a vassal.

label: Neither
summary: Whether neither of the two values is true.
details: It is true only when both values are false. Vanilla uses it in GUI files, for example to show an element only when a holy site is not held by the faith and a map mode variable is not set.

label: Neither (2)
summary: Whether neither of 2 values is true.
details: The same as Nor: it is true only when both values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: None of 3
summary: Whether none of 3 values is true.
details: It is true only when all three values are false. Vanilla uses it in GUI files, for example to hide an element when a lobby player is playable, an observer or joining mid-game.

label: None of 4
summary: Whether none of 4 values is true.
details: It is true only when all four values are false. Vanilla uses it in GUI files to show an element only when none of several variables or checks hold.

label: None of 5
summary: Whether none of 5 values is true.
details: It is true only when all five values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: None of 6
summary: Whether none of 6 values is true.
details: It is true only when all six values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: None of 7
summary: Whether none of 7 values is true.
details: It is true only when all seven values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: None of 8
summary: Whether none of 8 values is true.
details: It is true only when all eight values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Not
summary: The opposite of a true or false value.
details: True becomes false and false becomes true. Vanilla uses it thousands of times in texts and GUI files, for example to show a text only when something is not the case.

label: Not equal (decimal)
summary: Whether two decimal numbers are different.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tax collector texts, to add a line only when a value has actually changed.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Not equal (2D vector)
summary: Whether two two-part vectors are different.
details: A 2D vector is a pair of decimal numbers such as a screen position. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The vector it is compared with.

label: Not equal (3D vector)
summary: Whether two three-part vectors are different.
details: A 3D vector is three decimal numbers such as a position in space. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The vector it is compared with.

label: Not equal (4D vector)
summary: Whether two four-part vectors are different.
details: A 4D vector is four decimal numbers, for example a color with transparency. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The vector it is compared with.

label: Not equal (float)
summary: Whether two float numbers are different.
details: Vanilla does not use this exact function; going by its name, it is the float version of the not-equal check.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Not equal (whole)
summary: Whether two whole numbers are different.
details: Vanilla uses it in GUI files, for example to show an army element only when its maximum number of soldiers is not 0, or to skip the legitimacy level at the current list position.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Not equal (unsigned)
summary: Whether two unsigned whole numbers are different.
details: An unsigned number cannot be negative. Vanilla uses it to compare ids, for example to show something only when a culture or a nominee is not the same as another by id.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number it is compared with.

label: Is not zero
summary: Whether a whole number is anything other than zero.
details: It is a shortcut for a not-equal comparison with '(int32)0'. Vanilla uses it to show a panel only when it has at least one visible child element.

label: Is not zero (decimal)
summary: Whether a decimal number is anything other than zero.
details: It is a shortcut for a not-equal comparison with '(CFixedPoint)0'. Vanilla uses it to show parts of an activity widget only when a script value or variable is not 0.

label: Is not zero (long)
summary: Whether a long whole number is anything other than zero.
details: A long number is a 64-bit whole number. It is a shortcut for a not-equal comparison with '(int64)0'. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Error count
summary: A whole number the game shows after the word "Errors:" in a debug label.
details: Going by its name and that single use, it is a count of errors. The game documents nothing more.

label: Old relation level
summary: The level a house relation moves away from, in a text that also names the new one.
details: Vanilla's one use: the relation improves or worsens "from [old level] to [new level]".

label: Old law
summary: The law that was in force before a change, in a text about the change.
details: Vanilla's one use is a message that a law was changed "from [old law] to [new law]".

label: Organization
summary: An organization the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is the organization the window or text is about. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Replaced doctrine
summary: The doctrine a faith gives up when it takes a new one, in texts about the change.
details: Vanilla writes "Replaces [other doctrine] with [doctrine]". Where there may be no old doctrine, a text checks first whether it is set and otherwise uses the plain "Gains ..." text.

label: Objects are equal
summary: Whether two game objects are the same object.
details: Vanilla uses it constantly in texts and GUI files, for example to check whether a character's father is the same person as the real father, or whether a doctrine is a given one. Objects are sometimes passed with .Self.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a game object such as a character, doctrine or title

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The object it is compared with.
fields.values: a game object of the same kind

label: Create account
summary: Starts the account creation flow.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it on the login window's create-account button.

label: Slower game speed
summary: Lowers the game speed by one step.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it as the click action of two HUD buttons; going by its name, it slows the game down. The game documents nothing more.

label: Go to capital
summary: Moves the map view to the player's capital.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use in the HUD, it is the button that jumps to the capital. The game documents nothing more.

label: Faster game speed
summary: Raises the game speed by one step.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it as the click action of two HUD buttons; going by its name, it speeds the game up. The game documents nothing more.

label: Pause
summary: Pauses the game, going by its name.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it as the click action of three HUD buttons. Whether it also unpauses is not documented.

label: Open pause menu
summary: Opens the pause menu.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its single use in the HUD, it opens the in-game menu. The game documents nothing more.

label: Raise event troops
summary: Raises the event troops it is given.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it in the military window with a military view event troop entry. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The event troop entry to raise.
fields.values: an event troop item, usually .Self of the entry

label: Toggle login window
summary: Shows or hides the account login window.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use in the in-game menu, it opens or closes the login window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open achievements
summary: Opens the achievements window.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it on buttons in the in-game menu and the main menu.

label: Open administrative vassal view
summary: Opens the detail view of an administrative vassal for a title.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it on a map icon, passing the title. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The title whose administrative vassal is shown.

label: Open administrative army view
summary: Opens the detail view of an administrative army for a title.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it on map icons, passing the title. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The title whose army is shown.

label: Open character interaction
summary: Opens the window of a character interaction, aimed at a given character.
details: A button action. Going by its name and use: vanilla uses it in the Great Holy War window with the interaction 'select_ghw_beneficiary_interaction' and the player (GetPlayer) as second argument. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the interaction to open.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A character passed along with it; vanilla passes the player.

label: Open dynasty customization
summary: Opens the window for customizing a dynasty.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use in the dynasty and house window, passing the dynasty. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open error log
summary: Opens the game's error log.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use next to the error counter in a shared GUI component, it shows the logged errors. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open from view history
summary: Opens the window the player had open before, taken from the view history.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use in the character and confederation windows, it steps back to an earlier view. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open game rules
summary: Opens the game rules window.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it on buttons in the bookmark screen and the in-game menu.

label: Open game view
summary: Opens one of the game's windows by its name.
details: A button action. Going by its name, the argument names the window; vanilla uses it often, for example with 'cardinals_window' or 'move_domicile_planner'. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the window to open.
fields.values: a game view name in quotes

label: Open game view with data
summary: Opens one of the game's windows by its name and hands it the thing it should show.
details: A button action. Going by its name, it opens a window and hands it data. Vanilla uses it a lot, for example with 'government_administration' and a character, or 'lifestyle' and the player's id. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the window to open.
fields.values: a game view name in quotes

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The object or id the window should show.
fields.values: an object such as a character, or an id

label: Open GUI tab
summary: Switches a tab group to one of its tabs.
details: A button action. Going by its name, it switches a tab group to a tab; vanilla uses it in the HUD with 'dynastic_cycle_tabs' and the tabs 'dynastic_cycle' and 'movements'. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the tab group.

label: Open hireable ruler view
summary: Opens the detail view of a ruler who can be hired.
details: A button action. Vanilla uses it in the military window, passing a character.

label: Open house customization
summary: Opens the window for customizing a dynasty house.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use in the dynasty and house window, passing the house. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open mercenary company view
summary: Opens the detail view of a mercenary company.
details: A button action. Going by its name, it shows the given company. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Open set-acclaimed view
summary: Opens a view for setting someone as acclaimed.
details: A button action. Going by its name, it opens a view for setting something as acclaimed. The game documents nothing more, vanilla does not use it, and the kind of argument is unknown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The object the view is for.

label: Open title customization
summary: Opens the window for customizing a title.
details: A button action. Going by its name and its use in the county view and the title window, passing a title. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open title window and grant
summary: Opens a title window and starts granting a title.
details: A button action. Going by its name, it opens the title window for a title and has to do with granting it. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Or
summary: Whether at least one of the two values is true.
details: It is false only when both values are false. Vanilla uses it very often in texts and GUI files, for example to pick a text when a character is commanding an army or is a knight in one.

label: Or (2)
summary: Whether at least one of 2 values is true.
details: The same as Or: it is false only when both values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Or (3)
summary: Whether at least one of 3 values is true.
details: It is false only when all three values are false. Vanilla uses it in HUD files, for example to show an element when one of several windows is open or a hover variable is set.

label: Or (4)
summary: Whether at least one of 4 values is true.
details: It is false only when all four values are false. Vanilla uses it in windows, for example to show an element when a government has a mechanic or a law group has one of several flags.

label: Or (5)
summary: Whether at least one of 5 values is true.
details: It is false only when all five values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Or (6)
summary: Whether at least one of 6 values is true.
details: It is false only when all six values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Or (7)
summary: Whether at least one of 7 values is true.
details: It is false only when all seven values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Or (8)
summary: Whether at least one of 8 values is true.
details: It is false only when all eight values are false. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Perk
summary: The lifestyle perk a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name a perk a character gains or loses, written for that character.

label: Player message item
summary: A player message entry the game fills in for the text or window being shown.
details: Going by its name, it is one message in the player's message list. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Polish activity (accusative, tooltip)
summary: The name of an activity in the Polish accusative case, with a tooltip.
details: A helper for the Polish translation, which needs word endings that change with the sentence. It asks the activity for a custom text called PL_ActivityAccusativeStringBypass. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Polish activity (accusative)
summary: The name of an activity in the Polish accusative case, without a tooltip, with the host mentioned when it is not the player.
details: A helper for the Polish translation. The macro joins three parts, using the host's LocalPlayerString to choose: a possessive word ('your') for the activity type, the type's accusative name, and the words 'postaci' plus the host's short name. Going by that function's name, the possessive word is meant for the player's own activities and the host for other hosts; the game does not document it. Vanilla does not use it.
